headline: The S&P 500 rose 5.6% this week, its best Thanksgiving week since 2008, after Nvidia took Huang back. The rally has not been tested on a full session with volume yet, so Monday Nov 30 is the first day that can confirm it.
summary: All closes here are Friday Nov 27 (a half day that ended at 1pm ET), from Massive, and they match the dashboard. The S&P 500 closed at 7,297.49, up 1.60% Friday and 5.6% for the week; the Nasdaq rose 2.31% Friday and the Dow 1.18% to 50,774.94 (Barron's). SPY rose 5.58% for the week, QQQ 6.99% and NVDA 19.9% to 150.49, but NVDA added only 0.8% Friday after a 2.6% premarket gain, as the Bloomberg report on Blackwell chips in Shanghai sank in (Massive; CNBC). The VIX fell to 23.81 from 35.89 a week ago, while the 10 year yield ended near 4.94%, so bonds did not join the rally. Brent settled at $95.44, up about 3% for the week, and Reuters sources say OPEC+ will hold output steady on Sunday. Next week is crowded: ISM, JOLTS and jobs data, Huang before the House on Dec 1 and the Senate on Dec 3, the Fed's quiet period before the Dec 9 decision, and 23 hour trading from Sunday Dec 6.

regime.why: No change until a follow through day: a full session gain of about 1.5% or more on higher volume than the day before. Friday was a half day on light volume (most setups traded under half their normal volume), so it cannot count, even though IBD called it a follow through day 'in spirit'. Monday Nov 30 is the earliest full session that can give one. A December hike is still close to fully priced.

signals.title: Week in review: a 5.6% rebound led by the stocks that fell most, while bonds sat it out
signals.what_happened: Monday Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang at the White House's urging: NVDA rose 31% and SPY 4.7%. Tuesday HPE guided margins lower and ADI fell about 16% on its outlook. Wednesday core PCE came in hot at 3.3% and the US proposed Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies; the S&P 500 fell 3.2% intraday, then closed only 0.25% lower, and S&P put Nvidia's AA rating on watch for a cut. Thursday was closed. Friday was a half day: Asia and Europe had rallied, futures were up 1.7% before the open, and the S&P 500 closed up 1.60%. For the week (Massive, Nov 20 to Nov 27 closes): SPY +5.58%, QQQ +6.99%, IWM +6.69%, NVDA +19.9%, TSM +10.9%, SMH +10.0%, MU +8.8%. The biggest gainers on the dashboard were deal and drug names: KYMR +52%, ZS +22.9% (CrowdStrike deal), INSM +20.6% (Sanofi deal). What lagged: TLT -0.22%, INDA -0.25%, ADI flat, MDT -4.5%, CRWD -5.3%, NTNX -14.2%. Gold rose: GLD +3.57%.
signals.so_what: This was a relief rally after the worst week since 2020, led by the same AI names that crashed. Two warnings. First, bonds did not rally: the 10 year yield ended near 4.94%, about where it started, because a December hike is still priced. Stocks rising while yields stay high means the rally rests on earnings hopes, not on easier money. Second, the leaders faded late in the week: NVDA, MU and SMH all closed Friday below their Monday closes. What would make the rally real: a full session follow through day next week, and the chip leaders holding Monday's gains through Huang's Dec 3 hearing.
signals.for_you: Swing: no setup triggered this week; none of the eight setups closed over its entry on 1.5x volume. Puts: the VIX fell a third, to 23.81, so premiums are thinner than last week but still above normal. Long term: buy in small pieces only while the stance is risk off.

signals.title: Scorecard: how the calls did
signals.what_happened: The week's briefs, graded against Friday Nov 27 closes (Massive). No brief was published Nov 25, so there are four: Nov 23, 24, 26 and 27. A named stock counts as right when a beneficiary beat SPY, or a hurt name lagged SPY, from the brief's base close to Friday. Nov 23 (base Nov 20): 2 right, 6 wrong. Right: ZS +22.9% and CRWD -5.3% on the deal. Wrong: NVDA as hurt (+19.9%), INDA, HDB and IBN as helped (all lagged SPY's +5.6%), TLT as helped (-0.2%) and EWY as hurt (+10.2%). The stance, 'a premarket rally is not a bottom', meant waiting through a 5.6% week; that was the cost of the rule. Nov 24 (base Nov 23): 6 right, 4 wrong. Right: HPE (-11.0%), ADI (-8.6%) and DELL (-5.4%) as hurt, INSM (+14.3%) and KYMR (+16.7%) as helped, UAMY as hurt. Wrong: NVDA (-8.8%), TSM, MU and SMH as helped; the rally in them peaked that Monday. The action, 'no chip entries, these are bounces', was right. Nov 26 (base Nov 25, one session): 8 right, 7 wrong. The tariff hurt list mostly lagged (RDY, TM, HMC, PDD right; STLA +6.3% wrong); TLT as helped was wrong (-1.2%). Nov 27 (base Nov 25): 3 right, 4 wrong. NVDA as hurt (lagged at +0.8%), AMZN as helped (+4.0%) and NDAQ as helped (+1.9%) were right; XOM, CVX and OXY as helped and DAL as hurt were wrong, since Brent fell 1.2% Friday. Week total: 19 of 40 named calls right (48%). The 'no entries on Friday's half day' call was right: no setup reached its volume. Dashboard scorecard (site/data/scorecard.json, graded Nov 27): swings 43 calls, 5 finished, 3 wins (ABBV +0.25R, LNG +0.36R, BDX +0.86R) and 2 losses (EOG -1R, and WST -1R, stopped Friday at an intraday low of 364.20 under its 365.14 stop), average -0.11R, down from +0.12R; 21 never triggered and 17 waiting. Cash secured puts: 25 logged, 10 finished, 4 kept the premium, average -9.29%, 15 open; no new put ideas this week. Long term buys: 131 calls; 57 of 126 beat SPY after 5 days (45%, average 2.43 points behind) and 48 of 115 after 20 days (42%, average 3.71 behind). Brief signals: 138 of 261 right after 5 days (53%) and 80 of 148 after 20 days (54%, average 1.6 points ahead). My split of the 115 long term calls with 20 day results: the 35 in the AI compute and AI power maps averaged 18.52 points behind SPY and only 3 beat it; the other 80 averaged 2.77 points ahead and 45 beat it (56%).
signals.so_what: Small samples: 5 finished swings and 10 finished puts prove nothing yet. What works: the volume rule kept her out of setups that never confirmed, long term buys outside the AI groups beat SPY more often than not, and the 'wait' calls on chips this week were right. What does not work: bearish calls in a rebounding market (this week's hurt lists on chips and Korea were wrong), and long term buys in the AI groups, now behind for about eight weeks, which meets the routine's two month mark.
signals.for_you: One rule change to consider now: no long term buy call on a name in the AI compute or AI power maps unless the group itself is healthy (for example, SMH over its 200 day). Last week's open item, holding the scanner's put ideas to the brief's rules, still stands. Also: put a stock in 'hurt' only when the news changes who pays, not because its price is jumpy.

signals.title: Week ahead, Nov 30 to Dec 4: a test of the rally, Huang twice in Washington, then jobs
signals.what_happened: Sunday Nov 29: OPEC+ meets; three sources told Reuters it agreed in principle to keep first quarter 2027 targets unchanged. Monday Nov 30: Cyber Monday (Adobe forecast $15.1 billion online) and the first full session that can give a follow through day. Tuesday Dec 1: ISM manufacturing at 10am ET (forecast 55.0, prior 55.5) and JOLTS (forecast 7.46 million, prior 7.52 million) (Forex Factory, pulled Nov 27); Huang's closed door House interview (Politico); Marvell after the close (estimate $1.10 a share on $3.15 billion, Newsquawk). Wednesday Dec 2: Salesforce and Snowflake after the close (Newsquawk). Thursday Dec 3: Huang testifies to Senate Banking at 10am ET on export controls (Senate Banking); jobless claims 8:30am (forecast 195,000); ISM services 10am (forecast 54.5, prior 54.5). Friday Dec 4: November jobs at 8:30am ET (payrolls forecast 90,000, prior 165,000; unemployment 4.1%; hourly pay +0.3%, prior 0.4%). CrowdStrike and Zscaler also report this week (dates listed, not reconfirmed). The Fed is in its quiet period until the Dec 9 decision. Sunday Dec 6 at 9pm ET, 23 hour trading begins (Nasdaq).
signals.so_what: The rally has two tests. Data: an ISM over 55.5 with rising prices paid, or hourly pay over 0.4%, would lift January hike odds and yields. Washington: a hard Senate hearing on chips reaching China, after Friday's Blackwell report, could hit NVDA and the chip names that led the week. Marvell and Salesforce are the AI demand reads. Second order: with no Fed speakers, each number moves rates more than usual.
signals.for_you: Swing: a follow through day Monday or Tuesday would let her act on setups that then close over their entries on 1.5x volume (see actions); none reports before Jan 27. No chip entries before Dec 3. Puts: no CRWD, ZS, MRVL or CRM puts across their reports. Long term: no change; small pieces only.

signals.title: Nvidia: Huang's hearings are set for Dec 1 and Dec 3, and Friday's premarket gain mostly faded
signals.since_yesterday: NVDA closed up only 0.8% Friday after +2.6% premarket; Nvidia did not respond to Bloomberg, which said it has no evidence Megaspeed diverted the chips.
signals.what_happened: Bloomberg reported Friday that Blackwell hardware, which needs a US license to ship to China, appears in loan filings for a Shanghai data center linked to Megaspeed's founder; Bloomberg said it has no evidence Megaspeed diverted the hardware, and Nvidia did not respond (Bloomberg via mlq.ai). NVDA closed 150.49, up 0.8% Friday, after trading at 153.19 before the open (Massive; CNBC). Huang sits for a closed door House Foreign Affairs interview Dec 1 (Politico) and testifies in public to Senate Banking Dec 3 at 10am ET as the only witness (Senate Banking; The Hill).
signals.so_what: The stock gained about $600 billion in value this week on Huang's return (Yahoo Finance), and the next risk is what he says under oath about China sales. Who pays if Commerce tightens rules on overseas resellers: Nvidia, and clouds that rent chips to Chinese firms abroad. What would make this wrong: a calm hearing with no new findings, which would remove a cloud over the whole chip group.
signals.for_you: No action. NVDA has no buy point (under its falling 200 day at 202.43). No NVDA or chip puts before Dec 3.

signals.title: Oil: Brent fell Friday but rose 3% on the week; OPEC+ is set to hold output Sunday
signals.since_yesterday: Brent settled 1.2% lower at $95.44 Friday, and three sources told Reuters OPEC+ agreed in principle to hold first quarter 2027 targets.
signals.what_happened: Brent touched about $98 Friday, then settled down $1.13 at $95.44; it rose about 3% for the week, its first weekly gain in November. WTI settled at $83.08, down 0.7% (Reuters via mlq.ai; WSJ). Iraq says it is negotiating for a higher quota.
signals.so_what: A rollover is expected, so Sunday's meeting is unlikely to move oil much. The bigger driver is Iran: last week's attacks in Kuwait added the premium, and a deal or new strikes can move Brent $4 in a day. Friday's stock moves say oil is not driving these names right now: XOM, CVX and OXY lagged the S&P 500 and DAL beat it.
signals.for_you: Long term: DAL closed 84.82, at the top of its long term zone (85.19), so no chasing it. CVX has a ready pullback on the dashboard but closed 212.45, just under its 212.85 zone low, so treat it as not ready (see the data check). No energy swing setups.

history.what: Barron's says this was the best Thanksgiving week for the major indexes since 2008. In 2008 the big holiday rally came inside a bear market, and the S&P 500 did not make its final low until March 2009.
history.lesson: A sharp rally after a crash says sellers are tired, not that buyers are in charge. The rally has to hold through the next bad news.

history.what: The Fed kept hiking into strength; stocks fell almost 20% into Dec 24, 2018, and the bottom came when the Fed signaled a pause in January 2019.
history.lesson: In a hiking cycle the turn usually needs the Fed, not only cheaper prices.

cycle.differences: In 2008 credit was breaking and the Fed was cutting; today credit is working and the Fed is hiking. That makes a 2008 style collapse less likely, but it also means no Fed rescue is coming soon, closer to 2018.
cycle.for_you: Swing: act only after a full session follow through day, and then only on a close over the entry on 1.5x volume. Puts: premiums thinner than last week; no screen passed this week. Long term: small pieces only, and none in the AI groups until the group itself recovers.
